title: SecB Fail-Learn Common Definitions (WP1)
description: Shared $defs for the SECB-FAIL-LEARN-001 / SECB-FAIL-LEARN-P0-001 WP1 contract set (Failure Evidence Envelope, classification taxonomy, Experience Record, Knowledge Artifact, Skill Candidate, transitions). This is a NEW namespace under contracts/fail-learn/ -- it does not modify or replace the pre-existing generic contracts/evidence-envelope.schema.json, contracts/knowledge-claim.schema.json, or contracts/skill-manifest.schema.json, and it formalizes (does not silently replace) the informal v0.1 docs/templates/failure-evidence-envelope.yaml, docs/templates/knowledge-candidate.yaml, and docs/templates/skill-candidate.yaml. CROSS-FIELD AND CROSS-DOCUMENT LIMITATION: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12, without the non-portable $data keyword) cannot compare the VALUE of one property against a sibling property's value, and cannot resolve a $ref by ID across separate documents supplied out-of-band. Every such constraint named in the WP1 task (self-attestation detection, tenant lineage consistency, cross-document digest/lineage binding, transition-table legality, undeclared side-effect/permission detection) is enforced by the companion semantic-validator.mjs, not by this schema layer alone. Schema-only validation is never sufficient by itself for this contract set.

content_address_suffix.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 suffix used by content-addressed object ids (e.g. fev_<suffix>). The schema layer can only bound the SYNTAX of the suffix; it cannot recompute the digest over the sibling document to prove the id is genuinely content-addressed -- that recomputation is performed by semantic-validator.mjs (validateContentAddressIntegrity), which is also how it detects tampering (SCEN-04).

tenant_scope.description: Binds a record to its tenant/project/session boundary (SECB-FAIL-LEARN-001 section 14: 'Tenant A SHALL NOT read Tenant B records'). The schema layer requires the fields to be PRESENT; it cannot enforce that a consumer actually respects the boundary at read/write time (that is a runtime authorization concern, WP2/WP3), and it cannot prove a downstream record's scope was genuinely DERIVED from its declared upstream evidence rather than independently fabricated -- semantic-validator.mjs (validateTenantLineageConsistency) checks that derived records (Experience/Knowledge/Skill) declare the SAME tenant_id as the evidence they cite.

signature_envelope.description: Generic content-addressed signature binding, styled on in-toto Statement v1 / SLSA v1.2 provenance framing (source-validation doc item 7). The schema can require these fields to be well-formed; it CANNOT verify the cryptographic signature itself. That is out-of-band and out of WP1 scope -- semantic-validator.mjs only checks structural presence and that signed_digest matches the sibling document's recomputed canonical digest where the vector context supplies enough to do so, never real cryptographic verification.

failure_class.description: Closed failure ontology, SECB-FAIL-LEARN-001 section 5. Which classes count as positive-control (a correctly denied request, never a malfunction) is NOT fixed here -- it is data owned by classification-taxonomy.schema.json / data/classification-taxonomy.instance.json, so the taxonomy stays the single, versioned source of truth.

canonical_path.description: Bounded, root-anchored, forward-slash canonical filesystem path. Rejects traversal ('.', '..'), empty segments, trailing slash, backslash. Cannot resolve symlinks or verify workspace containment -- runtime concern, out of WP1 scope.

side_effect_class.description: Closed side-effect vocabulary for Skill Candidate manifests and test observations. CREDENTIAL_ACCESS is intentionally usable only as an OBSERVED value (test-case reporting) -- see skill-candidate.schema.json's declared_side_effects, which excludes it from the declarable set entirely, so any test case that observes it is structurally undeclared and always rejected (least-privilege by omission).

declarable_side_effect_class.description: Subset of side_effect_class that a Skill Candidate manifest is permitted to declare. CREDENTIAL_ACCESS is deliberately excluded.

action_class.description: Closed permission-class vocabulary, styled on the SecB auto-auth action_class enum (Package 018). Used both as the manifest's declarable permission set and as each test case's observed permission_class, so an undeclared permission_class is structurally detectable the same way an undeclared side effect is.

declarable_action_class.description: Subset of action_class a Skill Candidate manifest may declare at S0. Hard-deny classes (PROTECTED_BRANCH, RELEASE_DEPLOY, SECRETS_ACCESS, PRIVILEGE_ELEVATION) are structurally excluded -- least-privilege skill manifest, section 8.
